Keysight reported a record quarter, with earnings per share of $2.82 well above what had been expected and net income roughly doubling from a year earlier [C28]. Communications Solutions Group revenue grew by more than two fifths, and wireline revenue passed wireless revenue for the first time as AI data centre build-outs pulled demand for faster optical transceivers [C31] [C33]. Management now expects fourth quarter revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 [C1].

Demand runs far ahead of what the company can supply, and supply will govern near-term revenue for several quarters, so booked orders may not reach the income statement when the market expects [C34] [C40]. The fourth-quarter revenue range sits only slightly above the quarter just reported, and analysts questioned that modest sequential guide [C38] [C39]. A one-time tariff boost lifted profitability and will not repeat, which raises the bar margins have to clear [C18]. The market is arguing about whether the valuation leaves room for error after the guided step-up [C22] [C36].

The plan buys in three tranches at the support bands beneath the price, each an equal share of a full position [C13]. It sells an equal share at each traded resistance band above but the top one, and holds the last share on a stop trailed under the price from there [C14]. In an uptrend each tranche's stop is raised to the higher of the band beneath it and the last swing low beneath it [C15].
